LOCK SCOPE — the lock is per RUN DIRECTORY only. Nothing locks the workspace: two `jevcode` processes can start two different runs (two run dirs, two locks) on the same workspace realpath simultaneously and both edit the tree. gaps: No registry of LIVE sessions/runs: the only liveness signal is `<runDir>/run.lock` (pid+host), scoped to one run dir; there is no workspace-level lock, no `~/.jevcode/sessions/live/` or heartbeat, and the index's `live` flag is folded from run:start/run:end lines (index.ts:285) — a SIGKILLed process leaves `live:true` in the index forever until reindex. Two `jevcode` processes on the same workspace start two runs and both edit the tree with no detection, no warning, no heads-up (src/session/lock.ts, src/loop/engine.ts:459-468, :3097-3098).

Cross-device coordination is absent and the one lock rule is unsafe across devices: `lockIsLive` requires `lock.host === hostname()` (lock.ts:57), so with a synced or shared `~/.jevcode` (iCloud/Dropbox/NFS/SMB) machine B REPLACES machine A's live lock with only a jevcode.log warning (:117-125) and both processes then rotate the same state.json/state.prev.json (checksum mismatch → prev fallback → state.corrupt.json churn). `sessions unlock` (sessions.ts:111-114) can only judge same-host pids. `-c/--continue` picks the greatest lastUsed in the workspace regardless of which device is running it.

No per-session file ownership / claims / hand-off protocol: post/<step>.json records which files each step touched and run.json.git records HEAD, but nothing aggregates "session S is editing files F on branch B at commit C" for other sessions to read, and there is no message/note channel between sessions except seeding a follow-up inside one session (seed.ts). No hand-off message with a commit hash exists; run.json.git.head is the start-of-run oid only (plus resumedOn on resume).

No isolated worktree per session: the worktree pattern exists only for candidate lanes inside one run (lanes.ts) under `<runDir>/tmp/synth/`; a session always operates on the real workspace realpath, and a resume REQUIRES the identical realpath (resolve.ts:817-822) — a clone at a different path or on another machine cannot resume, and there is no relocation or `--workspace-moved` path.

Pause is a stop, not a suspension, and is not prompt: pause() is honoured only at the loop top after the in-flight step commits (engine.ts:1094), so an Esc during a 300 s generator call or a Jev retry chain waits; there is no `pause now and keep the draft/proposal for replay` (abort discards under rule 1 and re-buys the step), no pause of a whole session, no pause of a chat request, and a paused run has no resident state — `/resume` constructs a new engine (new lock, resumes+1). Nothing surfaces `pausing` to other processes.

Resume granularity is per committed step only: in-flight generator/Jev responses, the interrupted proposal (`state.interrupted.proposal`, display only), llm-jev sample bodies (source.ts:335-336 `a resumed step re-asks`) and a killed `run` command's partial effects are not resumable; there is no idempotency key or response cache keyed by (step, stage, prompt hash) to avoid re-paying after a crash.

Bench multi-process safety: `jevcode bench --resume <id>` has no lock on the bench dir or tasks.jsonl; two processes resuming the same benchId race on appends and the final atomic rewrite (runner.ts:435, :718-719); the per-pair IN_PROGRESS marker resumes with force:false, so a pair whose engine completed but whose final record never landed is refused as `already completed` rather than recorded.

Context is hard-bounded with no compaction: 4 steps × 600 chars of output, no summary of older steps, no persisted file-content memory between steps (jev-off/jev-only/llm-jev see only a candidate list; only jev-on's Jev context stage injects ≤12 files/60 KB), no visible context-usage meter, and the measured result is structural re-reading (baseline.md:224-231). No design doc (TUI-DESIGN, -2, -3) covers compaction or a generous-history mode; the bounds are duplicated in four places (window.ts:10-12, resume.ts:20-23, prompts.ts:15/:222/:230).

ui.json (composer draft + chips restored on resume) is specified in DESIGN.md:1568-1570 and TUI-DESIGN.md:1203-1205 and implemented in store.ts:545-554 but has no caller anywhere in src/ — drafts are lost on pause/exit/crash.

Picker `● live` from run.lock (TUI-DESIGN.md:1141, :1145; PickerOptions.live picker-lines.ts:37-38) is unwired: App.tsx:2094 passes the current process's phase; no code reads other runs' run.lock files.

No background notification between sessions: nothing watches `~/.jevcode/sessions/index.jsonl` or run dirs; a session learns of other runs only when it refolds the index at its own boundaries (open, /resume, run:end, budget:override). `--notify` exists for the local terminal only (TUI-DESIGN §14).

Stale-lock edge cases unhandled: pid reuse after a reboot makes a dead lock read as live (kill(pid,0) succeeds or EPERM → alive, lock.ts:26-35) and `sessions unlock` refuses it; a lock write failure leaves held=false so finish() never releases and the run is unprotected (engine.ts:465-467, :911-912); crash between store.create and takeRunLock leaves an unlocked, indexless run dir.

Run-dir growth is unmanaged: 800 run dirs on this machine; a bench run dir is 671 MB (tmp/synth lanes and sandbox-*.sb never GC'd); `sessions prune` only re-indexes; picker `x` moves to trash/ (never created yet); resume/picker cost and disk usage across devices are unaddressed.

Sub-agent (engine-internal parallel work) coordination is internal-only: llm-jev samples share one AbortSignal and per-sample wakers (engine.ts:964-976 sampleWakers), lanes serialise via withLane, but none of that is visible to the human as "what the sub-work is doing" beyond `synth` transcript lines, and none is resumable.
hazards: state.json is the SOLE truth on resume; steps.jsonl is folded only for step > state.step and plan/spend are never rebuilt from logs (resume.ts:5-8). Any multi-writer or cross-device design must keep exactly one writer per run dir, preserve tmp+fsync+rename with the prev rotation and the sha256 envelope (store.ts:361-383, :239-255), and keep envelope version 1 with optional-only field additions (TUI-DESIGN §8.10).

Lock acquisition/release are deliberately synchronous so the process 'exit' handler can release the lock (lock.ts:5; engine.ts:876-884). A heartbeat or registry write on the hot path must not become async I/O inside abort()/forceExit; the shutdown phase is bounded at SHUTDOWN_CHECKPOINT_BOUND_MS 5000 (engine.ts:214) after which state is written synchronously and the process exits.

`human_pause` is intentionally excluded from BUDGET_STOP_REASONS (stop.ts:9) and storedStopBlocks (engine.ts:809-826) so /resume needs no --force; index.ts:128-142 STOP_REASON_SET and :125 MODES are compile-time allow-lists — any new StopReason, EngineMode or IndexLine kind must be added there (and to INDEX_KINDS :36 and parseIndexBody :190-264) or lines are silently skipped by the fold.

Steer bounds (8 × 600) are defined once in src/core/types.ts:969-970 and consumed by the engine queue, Jev state.human and the prompt hints; changing them in one place changes Jev's request size (F7).

The seatbelt lets sandboxed commands write only under the workspace, `<runDir>/tmp` and `<runDir>/home` (lanes.ts:29-34); any new per-run coordination file must live outside those roots (or be treated as untrusted input) so a generator-proposed `run` cannot forge a registry entry, and secrets rules (redact on every artefact, ≤512 B index lines dropped not truncated) apply to any new line kind.

The checkpoint for step N overlaps step N+1 up to execute (engine.ts:2202): a "who is touching which files" record updated at commit lags the workspace by up to one step's pre-execute stages; pre-images are taken right before execute (:2220-2221) — that is the earliest point a file claim can be truthful.

`wallMsUsed` excludes paused time by construction (engine.ts wallMsUsed()); a session-level pause must not start the wall clock, and `resumes` increments per resume while the index folds a run:start with resumeOf as a resume (index.ts:323-329) — new hand-off/resume line kinds must keep that fold rule.

Bench and perf runs never write the index (index.ts:447) and have no blocker (every blocking pause answers 'stop'); a registry that assumes every run has an index line or an interactive answer will misbehave under bench concurrency (`--concurrency N` workers in one process, runner.ts:713).

Cross-provider resume re-keys resolvedJevModel via EQUIVALENT_IDS (engine.ts:704-716; resolve.ts:806-815); identity checks on resume are subtle — a cross-device design that changes provider/model defaults per device will hit `a resumed run keeps its …` ConfigErrors.

Window/clipping constants are duplicated in four files (window.ts:10-12, resume.ts:20-23, prompts.ts:15/:222/:230) and the Jev state carries the same `recent` (state.ts:113-123); relaxing context requires moving all copies together and re-measuring Jev request size (§5.5 `no Jev request is ever O(transcript)`).

Round-3 (docs/TUI-DESIGN-3.md) pins `/resume` aliases `r`, `sessions`, `continue` (:897) and makes the session follow `config.mode` including on `--resume` (:118); a sessions design must not reassign those aliases or re-introduce a mode mismatch (`--resume: run was a <mode> run`, engine.ts:3032).

The index writer relies on O_APPEND atomicity of ≤512 B lines (index.ts:460); that holds on local POSIX filesystems, not on NFS/SMB/synced folders — a cross-device design that syncs ~/.jevcode will tear lines (the fold skips them, counted in `skipped`).

A lock write failure sets held=false (engine.ts:465-467) and releaseLock then no-ops (:911-912); a registry built on run.lock inherits "unprotected but running" runs. Also pid liveness is host-local and pid-reuse-prone (lock.ts:26-35).

DISTRIBUTED LOCKING THEORY (Kleppmann, 'How to do distributed locking', 2016): a lease with a timeout is unsafe for correctness because 'Your processes will get paused' (GC, page faults, CPU contention, network delay) and wall clocks jump (NTP); the fix is a fencing token — a monotonically increasing number issued with every lock grant that the protected resource checks and 'rejects the request with token 33' once it has seen 34; distinguish locks for EFFICIENCY (duplicate work is only wasteful — a best-effort lock is fine) from locks for CORRECTNESS (needs consensus/fencing). For coding agents, a workspace/path lease is an efficiency lock; the git commit (`--force-with-lease`, index.lock) is the fencing point.

FILE LOCK IMPLEMENTATION PRIOR ART (node proper-lockfile README): uses `mkdir` for the lock because 'O_EXCL is broken on NFS file systems'; staleness is judged from the lockfile mtime (`stale` default 10000 ms, minimum 5000; `update` default stale/2, min 1000, max stale/2) and the holder keeps touching mtime; `onCompromised` fires when 'updates to the lockfile fail' or 'updates take longer than expected, possibly causing the lock to become stale'; it cannot detect manual removal; `realpath: true` by default; `retries` option. Mtime staleness is a cross-machine clock comparison, hence unreliable with skew.

POSIX/NFS (man 2 open): 'On NFS, O_EXCL is supported only when using NFSv3 or later on kernel 2.6 or later'; portable lockfile recipe: create a unique file (hostname+pid) then `link(2)` to the lock name; success if link returns 0 or the unique file's link count became 2. 'O_APPEND may lead to corrupted files on NFS filesystems if more than one process appends data to a file at once' because the client simulates append. This directly conditions JevCode's index.jsonl design (single O_APPEND write, no lock) on the home directory being a local filesystem.

MAILDIR (D. J. Bernstein; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maildir): lock-free mailbox = `tmp/`, `new/`, `cur/`; writer stats a unique name (`<time>.<pid>.<host>`, later `<time>.M<usec>P<pid>Q<count>R<random>.<host>` — hostname included precisely because several hosts may deliver into one shared directory), writes into `tmp/`, then `rename()`/`link()` into `new/` atomically; readers move `new/` → `cur/` adding `:2,<flags>`; files older than 36 hours in `tmp/` are garbage. 'designed ... with a major goal of eliminating the need for program code to handle file locking'. Directly reusable for a per-session inbox on a synced directory.

SYNC-FOLDER CONFLICT SEMANTICS: Syncthing renames the LOSER to `<name>.sync-conflict-<date>-<time>-<modifiedBy>.<ext>` where 'The file with the older modification time will be marked as the conflicting file'; ties broken by device id; conflict files propagate to all devices; temp files are `.syncthing.<name>.tmp`; deletion-vs-modification conflicts also produce a conflict copy. Dropbox creates `<name> (<user>'s conflicted copy <date>)` — 'The last version saved will always appear as the conflicted copy', neither version is dropped; triggered by simultaneous edits, offline edits, and files held open by auto-saving apps. Design consequence: any per-session artefact on a synced dir must be WRITE-ONCE with a name unique to the writer (Maildir style); a shared mutable file (index.jsonl, a lock file) WILL fork into conflict copies.

GIT WORKTREES (git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree): each linked worktree has `$GIT_DIR/worktrees/<id>/` with a `gitdir` file pointing at the checkout and a `.git` FILE in the checkout pointing back; `git worktree lock [--reason]` adds a `locked` file so `prune` never removes the entry ('portable device or network share which is not always mounted'); `git worktree prune` removes entries whose directories are missing, and `git gc` calls `git worktree prune --expire 3.months.ago` (gc.worktreePruneExpire, local man page git 2.50.1); `git worktree move` / `git worktree repair` re-link after a manual move of either side; 'By default, add refuses to create a new worktree when <commit-ish> is a branch name and is already checked out by another worktree' (`--force` overrides); `add -d/--detach` gives a throwaway detached checkout (what JevCode lanes use).

GIT LOCK TIMEOUTS (local `man git-config`, git 2.50.1): `core.filesRefLockTimeout` 'Default is 100 (i.e., retry for 100ms)'; `core.packedRefsTimeout` 'Default is 1000 (i.e., retry for 1 second)'; `gc.pruneExpire` default 2.weeks.ago 'helps prevent corruption when git gc runs concurrently with another process writing to the repository'. The index lock (`.git/index.lock`, or `<commonDir>/worktrees/<id>/index.lock` per worktree) has no retry knob — a second writer fails immediately with 'Unable to create ... index.lock: File exists. Another git process seems to be running'. `git --no-optional-locks status` (already used by JevCode, gitstate.ts:45) avoids taking index.lock for reads.

GIT AS A MAILBOX / CAS (git-scm.com/docs/git-push): `--force-with-lease=<refname>:<expect>` updates the remote ref only 'if the current value of the remote ref is the expected value ... git push fails otherwise' — 'like taking a lease on the ref without explicitly locking it'; `<expect>` empty means 'the named ref must not already exist' (create-if-absent); `--atomic` 'Either all refs are updated, or on error, no refs are updated'; bare `--force-with-lease` 'interacts very badly with anything that implicitly runs git fetch ... in the background'. A `refs/jevcode/sessions/<device-id>` ref per writer updated with CAS is a fencing-token-grade cross-device registry that rides the existing remote.

hazards: CORNER CASE — two devices sharing one run directory (e.g. `~/.jevcode` on iCloud/Dropbox/NFS): `lockIsLive` requires `lock.host === o.host` (lock.ts:57-59), so a lock from another device is `stale` and replaced with only a warning (lock.ts:101-103, 117-119). Two devices can therefore both 'own' one run and both append to steps.jsonl / rotate state.json — the exact split-brain the lock exists to prevent. Cross-host liveness must come from a lease (heartbeat + TTL judged in the READER's clock) plus a fencing epoch, never from hostname inequality.

CORNER CASE — pid reuse after a crash: `isPidAlive` treats EPERM as alive (lock.ts:33); after reboot or long uptime a recycled pid belonging to root or another user makes a dead run look 'in use' (exit 2) until the user runs `sessions unlock`, and conversely a recycled pid owned by the same user that is NOT jevcode also reads alive. Add process start time (or a boot id / `startedAt` vs `ps -o lstart`) to the lock so identity is (pid, start-time), not pid alone.

CORNER CASE — lock write failure is silent: `takeRunLock` returns `{held:false}` and the run continues without a lock when run.lock cannot be written (engine.ts:463-467). On EROFS/ENOSPC/NFS-hang two resumes of the same run can both proceed. Surface `held:false` in the status line and refuse a second unlocked resume of the same run id.

CORNER CASE — the append-only index on a network or synced filesystem: `appendFileSync` under O_APPEND with no lock (index.ts:1-7) is only atomic on local filesystems; open(2) documents O_APPEND corruption on NFS with concurrent appenders, and Dropbox/Syncthing turn a shared mutable `index.jsonl` into `index (conflicted copy)` / `.sync-conflict-` files that JevCode never reads. Per-device append-only files (`sessions/<device-id>.jsonl`) merged at read time are the safe shape; a single shared file is not.

CORNER CASE — clock skew between devices: index folding sorts by the writer's ISO `t` (index.ts ~560), `lastUsed = max t`, run ids embed writer wall time (run-id.ts:53-67), and Syncthing/proper-lockfile-style staleness compares mtimes across machines. A device 10 minutes fast makes its sessions 'most recent' forever and its leases look fresh after death; a device slow makes live leases look expired. Judge every lease from the observer's own receipt time ('I have seen this file unchanged for N intervals'), carry a per-writer monotonic sequence for ordering, and treat wall-clock only as display.

CORNER CASE — two sessions on the same repo PATH (no worktrees): today nothing prevents it — locks are per run dir, not per workspace, the index records `workspace` but nobody checks it, and Claude Code's own doc warns same-dir sessions 'can conflict if editing the same files' and that resuming one session in two terminals 'interleave[s] into one transcript'. A per-workspace advisory lease (`<commonDir>/jevcode.lock` or `~/.jevcode/workspaces/<repo-id>/lease`) with a visible 'another session (name, pid, host, since) is editing this checkout' banner and an explicit opt-in to proceed is the minimum; path-ownership claims are what make proceeding safe.

CORNER CASE — same repo via two clones/worktrees: sessions are invisible across them because the picker filters on exact realpath equality (picker-lines.ts:279) and `RunMeta.workspace` is an absolute path (types.ts:999); coordination artefacts keyed by path will not meet either. Git-level interactions still exist: shared refs (`filesRefLockTimeout` 100 ms, `packedRefsTimeout` 1 s), shared object store, one-branch-per-worktree refusal, and `git worktree prune`/`gc` run from ANY worktree removing registrations of lanes whose directories are on an unmounted volume. Key coordination by repo identity (realpath of `--git-common-dir` for local, root-commit sha + normalised remote URL for cross-device), the way OpenCode keys storage by project slug and Claude Code offers Ctrl+W 'all worktrees of the repository'.

CORNER CASE — a session paused with lane worktrees open: lanes are registered under `<commonDir>/worktrees/laneN` (lanes.ts:209-214) and are detached, so no branch is blocked, but (a) the lane checkout is frozen at the HEAD of pause time while the user keeps committing (only `resumedOn` warns on resume, engine.ts:3071-3077), (b) `git worktree list` in the user's terminal shows mysterious `lane0..laneN` entries, (c) a user's `git worktree prune` or `git gc` after 3 months removes a paused run's registrations if the run dir volume is unmounted, and (d) `jevcode sessions prune` / a manual `rm -rf ~/.jevcode/runs/<id>` leaves dangling registrations until the next `git worktree prune`. Claude Code's pattern applies: `git worktree lock --reason 'jevcode run <id> paused'` while a run is paused/running, a marker so sweeps never touch user worktrees, and release of locks whose owning process is dead.

CORNER CASE — killed mid-step (SIGKILL, OOM, power loss) with a lease held: the 'exit' handler never runs, so state.json may lack the rule-1 `interrupted` record until `foldStepsIntoState` reconstructs from steps.jsonl (resume.ts:143-183), run.lock stays (recoverable same-host only), lane worktrees stay registered, and any path-ownership claims or heartbeat files stay 'fresh' until their TTL lapses. On another device the run keeps looking live until the lease expires; if the TTL is long (Claude's Remote Control tolerates ~30 min of failed presence heartbeats) the user waits. Design the TTL short (tens of seconds) with a visible countdown, and make claims re-validated (fencing epoch) on every write so a resurrected process cannot overwrite a newer owner.

CORNER CASE — a device offline for hours returns with stale state: its lease and path claims have expired and may have been reclaimed; its outbox messages are late (Claude Code delivers to `offline` sessions 'only after that session's machine reconnects'); its checkpoint references a HEAD that may be rewritten or a branch that was merged/deleted (Claude's reuse rule detects 'merged and remote branch deleted' from git state alone). The returning session must re-read the registry, compare its epoch with the current one, and downgrade to 'read-only until re-claimed' rather than resuming edits; late messages must carry the sender's epoch so receivers can discard superseded heads-ups.

CORNER CASE — the shared directory is unavailable or half-present: iCloud evicts to `.icloud` stubs, Dropbox pauses offline, NFS/SMB stat() can HANG the Node event loop (synchronous `readFileSync` in `readRunLock`, lock.ts:50, and the `'exit'` handler's `rmSync`). `classifyDiskError` knows ENOSPC/EACCES/EROFS/EDQUOT/EIO/EMFILE but not ESTALE/ETIMEDOUT/ENOTCONN/EHOSTDOWN (store.ts:60). Coordination I/O must be off the engine's critical path (worker/async with a deadline), degrade to a visible 'solo — coordination dir unreachable since <t>' mode, and never block a step, a pause, or an exit.

CORNER CASE — concurrent git operations: two agents in the SAME worktree race on `index.lock` (fails immediately, no retry knob) and on the working tree itself (JevCode's `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- <paths>` undo, git.ts:222-236, would revert another agent's uncommitted edits to the same paths); two agents in DIFFERENT worktrees share refs/packed-refs (100 ms / 1 s retry) and object packs (safe) but a `gc` in one can race a write in the other (gc.pruneExpire grace exists for this). Serialise same-worktree git writes behind the workspace lease, retry ref-lock failures with jitter, and never delete a foreign `index.lock` unless its holder pid is provably dead on this host.

CORNER CASE — resume of a run whose workspace moved or was re-cloned: fails with 'is not the run's workspace' (resolve.ts ~822-828) or, without `--workspace`, silently targets the OLD absolute path (session.ts:2044) — which may now be a different checkout or nothing; the run's lanes' `.git` files still point at `<old>/.git/worktrees/laneN` (fixable by `git worktree repair` from the new location). Copy Claude Code's binding logic: verify identity (commonDir realpath / root commit), offer re-binding to the launch directory with an explicit message, record the re-binding in run.json, and clear a binding whose directory is gone.

CORNER CASE — secrets in coordination artefacts: registry rows, heartbeats, mailbox messages and hand-off notes are the first JevCode artefacts that would leave the machine (synced folders, a git remote, a relay), and messages naturally quote command output. Every string must pass the existing Redactor (redact.ts:33-50) AND the composer's `detectSecrets` gate before write; a `.worktreeinclude`-style copy of `.env` into lanes/worktrees must never be automatic; a git-mailbox ref pushed to `origin` is visible to every collaborator with read access; Remote Control-style relays persist transcripts server-side. OpenCode's `export --sanitize` and Claude's 'plain text only, never history or files' rule are the precedents.

HAZARD — mailbox poisoning: one malformed entry in a shared JSON inbox blocked delivery for the whole mailbox in Claude Code before v2.1.207. Use one-file-per-message (Maildir) so a bad message is skipped individually, validate on read, quarantine (`cur/bad-…`) instead of deleting, and cap per-message size (Claude refuses ~1M chars at the sender).

HAZARD — message storms and loops between agents: without receiver-side rate limits, identical-repeat suppression and a bounded queue (Claude: 50 queued, 100 held, per-sender rate limit) two agents that acknowledge each other's acknowledgements never stop; with `notify_when_idle`-style subscriptions, a forgotten subscription must expire (Claude: 12 h).

HAZARD — treating an inter-agent message as authority: a heads-up or hand-off from another session must never satisfy a permission gate, change config/instruction files, or run slash commands embedded in its text; Claude Code labels the sender, strips `@` attachments, and holds messages from bypass-permission senders. JevCode's trust gate for AGENTS.md (session.ts trust lines) is the analogous boundary to extend.

HAZARD — hostname as device identity: `os.hostname()` is not stable (macOS `.local` vs DHCP-assigned names, VPN changes) and not unique (two 'MacBook-Pro.local'); using it in leases (lock.ts:57) misclassifies liveness both ways. Persist a random device id under `~/.jevcode/device.json` (never synced) and keep hostname as a display label.

HAZARD — a background/-p (non-interactive) run leaves locks: Claude Code documents that `-p` worktree sessions keep their `git worktree lock` until a later sweep; JevCode bench/perf sources (`source: 'bench' | 'perf'`, types.ts:1024) skip the index entirely (index only written when `source === 'cli'`), so bench runs on the same repo are invisible to the coordination layer while still holding lanes. Register every source in the registry, mark it `kind: bench`, and give sweeps the pid/start-time to release dead holders.

HAZARD — engine parallelism inside one session (lanes) vs cross-session claims: a lane candidate runs tests in a detached checkout of HEAD, so another session's uncommitted edits to the same files are invisible to it and its verdict can be stale the moment the other session commits; path claims must be checked at candidate ACCEPT time (when `applied` becomes a working-tree edit), not at lane creation, and a claim conflict should downgrade the verdict to 'needs re-verify' rather than block the lane pool.

HAZARD — pause is not instantaneous and never mid-command: `pause()` waits for the loop top (engine.ts:1094); a long test command keeps running and keeps the lease; a second device seeing 'paused' in the registry while the process still holds the lane worktrees and is still writing the checkpoint will act on stale truth. Publish a three-state `pausing → paused` transition with the step number and the lane count still busy, and keep the lease alive until `finish()` has written the final state.

HAZARD — the seatbelt writable set does not include a shared coordination directory: allowed writes are ws, run tmp/home, extra roots and git dirs (seatbelt.ts:92-104); the jevcode home is read-DENIED to sandboxed children (seatbelt.ts:164). Coordination writes must therefore happen in the harness process (fine) — but any design that lets a sandboxed command 'post a note' to the mailbox (Claude exposes `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` to Bash) needs an explicit allow rule for one socket or one directory, not a general widening.

HAZARD — case-insensitive and symlinked paths in identity keys: macOS APFS is case-insensitive by default; `realpath` is already used for run dirs and workspace (run-id.ts:102, session.ts:3224), but a coordination key derived from `commonDir` must also be realpath'd and normalised, or the same repo yields two keys (`/Users/x/Proj` vs `/users/x/proj`, `~/Documents` vs `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/...`).

HAZARD — compaction and coordination: if JevCode adopts OpenCode-style pruning of old tool outputs, hand-off messages and ownership claims received earlier in the session are exactly the 'old tool outputs' that get pruned; keep coordination state (who owns what, last heads-up per peer, pending hand-offs) in a structured side-channel that is re-injected after compaction, the way Claude Code re-injects CLAUDE.md, skills and the five most recently modified files.
reusable: Lease-file format to standardise across JevCode (per session, one write-once-then-rewritten file, never a shared file): `{ v, sessionId, runId, deviceId (random, persisted in ~/.jevcode/device.json, never synced), host (display only), pid, pidStart (process start time for pid-reuse defence), epoch (fencing token: max(existing epochs)+1 at every (re)claim), seq (per-writer monotonic counter), state: starting|running|pausing|paused|ended|crashed, step, stage, workspaceKey, branch, head, ownedPaths[], busyLanes, writtenAt (writer wall clock, informational), ttlMs }`. Written with tmp+rename (src/core/atomic.ts:19-38) to `<coord>/sessions/<deviceId>-<sessionId>.json`; readers judge liveness as `now_local - firstSeenUnchangedAt > ttl`, never from `writtenAt`.

Local liveness = JevCode's existing O_EXCL + EEXIST-re-read + tmp/rename pattern (src/session/lock.ts:91-126) extended with (pid, pidStart) identity; cross-device liveness = heartbeat lease judged in the observer's clock + fencing epoch. Keep `run.lock` for 'same run, same host' exclusion (it is correct and tested), and ADD a per-workspace lease keyed by repo identity for 'same checkout, any run'.

Repo identity key (for both the picker's 'all worktrees of this repo' widening and cross-device coordination): `sha256(realpath(--git-common-dir))` locally, plus `rootCommit = git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD | head -1` and a normalised `origin` URL for cross-device matching; store all three in RunMeta.git (types.ts:796-804 already has `RunGitMeta`) and index rows; fall back to `realpath(workspace)` for non-git workspaces (OpenCode's `project/<slug>/` vs `project/global/` split).

Path-ownership manifest (the 'per-session ownership of files' the user wants): each session publishes `ownedPaths` as gitignore-style globs in its lease file; before an edit the engine checks every OTHER live lease for an overlapping claim and emits a `heads-up` message (see mailbox) when it must touch a claimed path; claims are advisory (efficiency lock per Kleppmann) with the git commit as the fencing point; conflicts render as a status-line badge and a picker column, mirroring Claude Code's 'each teammate owns a different set of files' and TUI-DESIGN-3 §7's 'every file has exactly one owner ... sends the request'.

Maildir-shaped mailbox on any medium (local disk, synced folder, or a git ref): `<coord>/inbox/<toSessionId>/{tmp,new,cur}/`, message file name `<seq>.<deviceId>.<sessionId>.<random>.json`, write into `tmp/` then rename into `new/`; receiver renames `new/→cur/` after reading; malformed files are moved to `cur/bad/` not deleted; `tmp/` entries older than 36 h are garbage. Works without locks and survives Dropbox/Syncthing because every file is written once by one writer.

Message envelope: `{ v, id, from:{sessionId, deviceId, name}, to, kind: heads-up|hand-off|request|ack|idle-notice|shutdown-request|shutdown-ack, epoch, seq, sentAt, ttlMs, body (redacted plain text ≤ cap), refs: { commit?: sha, paths?: [], runId?, step? } }` — hand-offs carry the commit hash and changed paths (the user's 'hand-off messages with commit hashes'); receivers discard messages whose `epoch` is older than the sender's current epoch; commands in `body` are never executed; body passes the Redactor and `detectSecrets` before write.

Delivery guarantees to implement (copied from Claude Code cross-session messaging): read between steps, never mid-command; idle receiver starts a turn / shows the message; outcomes delivered | held | refused with a notice back to the sender; caps: message size, per-sender rate, identical-repeat suppression, queue ≤ 50, held ≤ 100; `notify_when_idle`-style one-shot subscription with a 12 h expiry; sending to self refused; an `offline` peer accepted for late delivery with the sender told so.

Inbound trust controls: `coordination.inbound = accept | hold | refuse` (default `hold` when the sender runs with fewer gates than the receiver), plus `coordination.isolateDevices = true` to require confirmation before anything leaves the machine; incoming text is labelled 'from session X on device Y' in the transcript and can never answer a blocking pane, trust gate or secret-ack.

Registry read model for the TUI/CLI (`jevcode sessions` and the picker): fold all `<coord>/sessions/*.json` + per-device index files into rows `name │ device │ state │ step/stage │ owned paths │ last heartbeat (Ns ago, judged locally) │ head`; mark rows `offline` when the lease aged out, `crashed` when a same-host pid is dead, `stale-epoch` when a newer claim exists; expose `jevcode agents --json` for scripts (Claude: `claude agents --json`) rather than parsing files.

Worktree hygiene for lanes (the engine's subagents): `git worktree lock --reason 'jevcode run <id> (<state>)'` on every lane after `add --detach`, unlock in `disposeLanes`; write a `jevcode` marker file into `<commonDir>/worktrees/laneN/` so a sweep only touches JevCode-created worktrees; a `jevcode sessions sweep` that unlocks/removes lanes whose (pid, pidStart) is dead and whose run is `ended|crashed`, and never touches user-created worktrees (Claude Code v2.1.210/v2.1.246 rules); show lanes as `lane worktrees: N (locked)` in the pause message.

Per-session isolated worktree option (Claude `--worktree`): `jevcode --worktree <name>` → `<repo>/.jevcode/worktrees/<name>` on branch `jevcode/<name>`, base `fresh` (origin default) or `head`, `.jevcodeinclude` to copy gitignored files deliberately (default OFF for anything matching SECRET_NAME_RE, redact.ts:56), exit prompt keep/remove based on dirty/unpushed state, resume re-enters after verifying `.git` file → `<commonDir>/worktrees/<name>` and clears the binding when the directory is gone.

Pause/resume/end contract, high detail: states `starting → running ⇄ pausing → paused → running` and `→ ending → ended|crashed`; every transition writes the lease (state, step, stage, busyLanes) BEFORE the transcript line; `pausing` persists until `finish('human_pause')` has written state.json; `paused` leases have a long TTL (they are legitimately idle) but still carry pid/pidStart so 'paused but process gone' reads as `crashed`; `/resume` from another device is allowed only when the lease is `paused|ended|crashed` or expired, and takes epoch+1; `/end` (new) = pause + release claims + unlock lanes + write `ended` + optionally `git worktree remove` clean lanes; `/handoff <session|device>` = pause + hand-off message with head sha, changed paths and `resume` command line.

Crash/offline detection matrix: same host → `kill(pid,0)` + pidStart match (authoritative, immediate); other device → lease age judged locally (probabilistic, TTL = 3×heartbeat, heartbeat default 10 s locally, 60 s on synced dirs); a returning writer compares its epoch to the registry and, if superseded, enters read-only 'superseded' mode and asks the user; on resume of a `crashed` lease the engine already folds steps.jsonl (resume.ts:143-183) — add 'last heartbeat at step N stage S' to the transcript so the user sees where it died.

Cross-device transport options, ranked for JevCode: (1) synced directory (iCloud/Dropbox/Syncthing) — zero infra, works with the Maildir/write-once shapes above, latency seconds-to-minutes, needs the 'shared dir unavailable' degrade path; (2) git-based mailbox — `refs/jevcode/sessions/<deviceId>` and `refs/jevcode/inbox/<sessionId>` updated with `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expect>` (CAS, `<expect>` empty for create) and `--atomic`, rides the existing remote and SSH auth, fenced by construction, but pushes are visible to all collaborators (redaction mandatory) and latency = poll interval; (3) tiny relay — outbound-only HTTPS long-poll like Claude Remote Control, best latency and offline queues, but new infra, credentials and server-side retention.

Compaction/context settings modelled on OpenCode and Claude Code for requirement (3): `context.autoCompact` default true; `context.reservedTokens` buffer so compaction itself cannot overflow; `context.prune` default false with `PRUNE_PROTECT`=40k recent tool-output tokens never pruned and `PRUNE_MINIMUM`=20k reclaimable before pruning runs; `preserveRecentTokens` = clamp(25 % of usable, 2k, 15k); a `/context` breakdown and a status-meter percentage (visible usage); `/compact [focus]` manual; re-inject after compaction: instructions files, the coordination side-channel (owned paths, peers, pending hand-offs), and the N most recently changed files (Claude: 5, files > 5k tokens as path refs); `JEVCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT` env; explicit 'resume from summary vs full' choice for stale large sessions.

Secret hygiene rules for every coordination artefact: run `redactor.redact` + `detectSecrets` on every string before it is written to a lease, index row or message (the store already does this for checkpoints, store.ts:7-8); never copy `.env`/key files into lanes or worktrees automatically; keep `device.json` (device id) and any relay credential in `~/.jevcode/` which the seatbelt already denies to sandboxed children (seatbelt.ts:164) and which must be EXCLUDED from any synced/coord directory; refuse to place the coordination dir inside the workspace or inside a directory that is itself a git checkout pushed to a remote unless the user opts in; a `jevcode sessions export --sanitize` twin of OpenCode's.

Ownership/hand-off conventions to write into the design (copied from how the Claude sessions coordinate this repo today, r3-implement.js:16 and TUI-DESIGN-3 §7): exclusive file lists per agent; cross-owner changes are REQUESTS carried in the report/hand-off, not edits; no concurrent build/perf/pty runs — model as a named shared resource (`build`, `pty-tests`, `perf`) claimable in the lease exactly like a path; final messages are data (files, tests, numbers, deviations, requests, problems) — make the hand-off message schema carry those fields.

Test matrix the design should demand (each a vitest unit with injected clock/pid/fs): two processes racing an empty lease (EEXIST re-read wins once); dead pid with recycled pid + different pidStart; other-device lease within TTL vs past TTL judged by local clock with ±15 min writer skew; a writer returning with an old epoch; conflicted-copy file names in the coord dir ignored; torn/malformed message quarantined without blocking others; message loop terminates within the caps; lane lock survives `git worktree prune`; resume with moved workspace offers re-binding and repairs lane `.git` files; secret string in a heads-up is redacted before the file exists on disk (assert via injected fs).

Plan bounds and bloat (src/loop/plan.ts:10-20): PLAN_MAX_ITEMS 20 × 200 chars, PLAN_MAX_CLAIMS 8, open problems 16, harness problems 16; rule (b) drops a `remaining` item only with a replan, a human directive, or new_information ≥ 0.7 (:186) — 2/40 live judge answers reached 0.7 (map row 9), so `plan.remaining` grew to 10 while the generator's own draft listed 1–3 (DESIGN §17 'Plan retention bloat'). The plan section is rendered in full every step (prompts.ts:141-158) and sent to Jev every request (state.ts:102-111).

Checkpoint image limits (src/checkpoint/images.ts:37-46): PRE_IMAGE_MAX_FILE_BYTES 1 MiB (larger files recorded as skipped 'size', never copied), PRE_IMAGE_MAX_FILES 200 and PRE_IMAGE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES 16 MiB for the dirty set before a `run` (edit/write/patch targets uncapped), POST_IMAGE_HASH_CAP_BYTES 16 MiB per step (files past it get sha256: null and /undo asks), POST_IMAGE_CHUNK_BYTES 4 MiB ≈ 2.4 ms sha256 per chunk with a setImmediate yield; imagesMs p95 measured 19.4 ms against a 15 ms target, inside harnessMs.

Perf gates that bound any in-process context work (docs/DESIGN.md §12): harnessMs p95 < 50 ms per step (measured 46.0 ms p95 with images included — ~4 ms headroom), first frame < 300 ms cold p95 with zero network and no config read before the frame, event-loop lag p95 < 5 ms / max < 50 ms under the TUI. Redaction cost: 51 exact secret entries make `redact` ~5× slower on 256 KB (1.6 ms) (docs/research/tui/00-SUMMARY.md:401); `redact` is split/join per entry then 6 format patterns + header pattern (src/core/redact.ts:68-78, :118-124), MIN_SECRET_LENGTH 8 (:53).

Redaction must cover every new prompt/state surface: context files (context.ts:109), read output (execute.ts:79), run stdout/stderr (execute.ts:107), Jev states (state.ts:147, :214, :506), the proposal rawText (propose.ts:49), every emitted event (engine.ts emit → redactDeep), every checkpoint write (store.ts:152-160) and transcript line (store.ts:506). Secrets added via addSecret mid-session are process-scoped and do not survive --resume (TUI-DESIGN §10.2, P56).

Visible usage today: the status line shows cumulative tokens `gen 5.5k jev 28k` only at ≥ 160 columns (src/tui/status/lines.ts:144, :432-441; jev-only `jev 28k`; under --allow-unpriced `gen 43.1k/133k tok`), spend meters `run $1.60/2.00` at ≥ 80 columns, and `/cost` is a ≤ 12-row block of spend, per-step p50, gen/jev split and pricing basis (docs/TUI-DESIGN.md:1237-1239). No per-prompt size, no percent-of-context-window, and no per-model context_length table exists (the 1,310,720 figure lives only in a comment, defaults.ts:70). Budgets: BUDGET_ORDER spend_cap → token_cap → wall_time → max_steps → max_replans (src/loop/budget.ts:11); token_cap fires only under --allow-unpriced (:45-48).

Synthesizer-side context in jev-only/llm-jev (docs/JEV-ONLY-DESIGN.md §2.1, §5.2; docs/LLM-JEV-DESIGN.md §4.4, §4.11): SearchMemory (baseline, goals, tried set, localizeCache, widenCursor, committed) lives in memory with durable copy = `plan.remaining` fixed-form items + the workspace; synthState persists `tried`/`widenCursor` and the LLM round cache `{goalId: {round, sha12[]}}` ≤ 4 KB (sample bodies not persisted; a resumed step re-asks ≈ $0.003). The llm-jev fix prompt is 3–6k tokens with every section bounded by PROMPT_LIMITS_FIX (src/synth/llm/prompt.ts:16-34: ≤ 4 listings × 120 lines, task head 3,000 + tail 1,000, ≤ 6 earlier attempts × 600 chars) and deliberately has 'no plan, no intent, no window of prior steps'.

opencode reference behaviour (fetched 2026-09-21, opencode.ai/docs): config `compaction: { auto: true ("Automatically compact the session when context is full"), prune: false ("Remove old tool outputs to save tokens"), reserved: 10000 (token buffer left for the compaction itself) }`; `/compact` alias `/summarize` (ctrl+x c); `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT`; `/sessions` alias `/resume` `/continue` (ctrl+x l); CLI `--continue/-c`, `--session/-s`, `--fork`; `session list -n --format`; `export [id] --sanitize` / `import <file>`. The model is: keep the full transcript, summarise automatically only near the model's limit, optionally prune old tool outputs, and expose compaction as a command.

Intent/context Jev stages are serial and cost ~200 ms each (map rows 2-3; context cannot start until intent resolves because the question text embeds the intent); the judge state is rebuilt with a provisional window entry for the current step (engine.ts:2240-2241 pushWindow(this.window, provisionalEntry)), and `recentOutputAt` (state.ts:428-437) returns null once a step leaves the 4-entry window — which is why `lastTestRunOutput` exists as a backstop for `done` judging (:457).
gaps: No file-content memory: the jev-on context stage re-selects and re-reads files each step (context.ts:83-119) and jev-off / llm-jev-generic never inject file contents at all (engine.ts:2128-2131, prompts.ts:279-280); the generator has no way to see a file it read two steps ago except a new `read` (baseline finding 3). A design must define a per-run file cache keyed by path with the version (mtime/sha) it showed, invalidated by changedFiles after edit/write/patch/run and by the candidate refresh after `run`.

No history beyond 4 steps in any form: no rolling summary, no compaction, no on-disk transcript the generator can reach. steps.jsonl holds StepRecords but not `read` outputs (execute.ts:80 — no exec on read) and not raw generator replies (types.ts:1032-1050), so a 'full history on disk' design needs a new per-step artefact (e.g. `<runDir>/outputs/<step>.txt`, redacted, bounded by the 200 KB sandbox cap and the 60 KB read cap).

No context meter: nothing reports the size of the last prompt, its share of the model's context window, or how much of it is window vs files vs plan; there is no per-model `contextLength` beside PRICING_TABLE (defaults.ts:81-84) and `tokensText` shows only cumulative totals at ≥ 160 columns (lines.ts:432-441). GeneratorCallRecord.usage already carries per-call input/cacheRead tokens to drive one.

Compaction trigger and output are undefined: no `contextBudget` setting, no step-count trigger, no field in CheckpointState for a summary (only `synthState`, which in jev-only/llm-jev is the synthesizer's and is silently dropped over 64 KiB, engine.ts:1805-1806), no `/compact` command in docs/COMMANDS.md, and no transcript/`--json` item type for 'compacted N steps'.

The 160,000-char hard cap on the user message cuts the middle of the message with a `…[N chars omitted]…` marker (prompts.ts:286) — invisible to the user and unrecorded except through promptChars; a generous design needs a per-section budget with a visible 'dropped' note (TUI item + steps.jsonl field) instead of a whole-message headTail.

In-memory context lost on --resume without a design note: `lastTestRunOutput` (engine.ts:597, :2699), PatchHistory (map row 5), the synthesizer's tried/testedSites. Any new cache or summary needs a fold path equivalent to foldStepRecord (window.ts:74-91) or must be re-derivable from disk (files: re-read; outputs: from steps.jsonl exec or the new outputs artefact).

Follow-up seeding (seed.ts:10, :62-64) carries only 4 window entries; a summary / file cache / outputs index would not carry into a follow-up run unless the seed contract (TUI-DESIGN §8.3) is extended — and pinnedFiles is the only human-controlled context carry today.

Jev state total size is unbounded in code (per-field STATE_LIMITS only, state.ts:30-41). The map's '300 candidates ≈ 60k tokens' for one context request (docs/STATUS.md:266) is not reconcilable with Jev's published context_length 32,000 (docs/research/07-generator-apis.md:174) — either the figure is per step across requests or the client tolerates more than the metadata says; verify against jev.jsonl before sizing any Jev-side keep/drop question.

Plan bloat (DESIGN §17; plan.ts:186-197) is a context problem with no compaction rule: retained items accumulate up to 20 × 200 chars in every prompt and every Jev state; a text-normalisation or age-expiry rule is listed as a candidate but not designed.

opencode parity items with no counterpart: auto-compaction with a reserved buffer, `prune` of old tool outputs, `/compact`, `--fork` on resume (JevCode has `/resume --force` and follow-up seeding, but no fork of a run mid-history), `export --sanitize` of a session (JevCode has `/export <file>` of the transcript; TUI-DESIGN §15).
hazards: Jev must stay bounded while the generator gets generous: Jev's context_length is 32,000 tokens and latency grows with state (30k → 372 ms; state.ts:1-4 'no Jev request is ever O(transcript)'). Any long history, file cache or summary must be generator-only (PromptInput) and never enter buildCommonState's `recent`/`plan` (state.ts:125-148) — otherwise 3–5 Jev requests per step each pay the size and the risk stage (fail-closed) slows every action.

Cost asymmetry by provider: 60 KiB of cached file text ≈ 15k tokens is $0.002/step on GLM served ($0.15/M) but $0.03/step on Sonnet 5 ($2/M input, $0.2/M cache read) — a context policy must be sized from `config.generator.pricing` and the model's context length, not a constant; the $0.25 jev-only default cap and $2 default cap (defaults.ts:12-14) bound total steps.

Prompt caching is prefix-based: today only system+tools are stable (anthropic.ts:87, :98). Placing a growing file cache or history after the volatile plan/intent/hints sections makes it uncacheable; placing it before them changes the prompt layout that the flat-tokens test and promptChars (propose.ts:27) and `promptHash` (types.ts:1035) pin. Reorder deliberately: stable → volatile.

GLM's `length` stops at 4,096 output tokens (27 % malformed) are independent of prompt size; a larger prompt with reasoning on does not reduce them and each retry re-sends the whole (now larger) prompt — both attempts are metered (propose.ts:44-60). Budget the retry as 2× prompt cost when sizing.

Redaction is O(prompt × secrets) per step (redact.ts:118-124): a full-history transcript re-redacted every step is O(history); a 60 KiB cache with 51 exact entries costs ≈ 0.4 ms (1.6 ms / 256 KB) — acceptable; a 1 MB history is not inside the 50 ms harness gate. Redact once at capture (as context.ts:109 and execute.ts:79 do) and store redacted bytes; never re-redact.

Checkpoint growth: state.json is rewritten with fsync every step (DESIGN §9); putting a file cache or history into CheckpointState multiplies write bytes per step and the harness p95 is already 46 of 50 ms. Persist only indices (paths, sha/mtime, step shown, byte counts) in state.json; keep bodies in append-only artefacts or re-read from the workspace on resume.

Stale cache correctness: a cached file view shown after the file changed (own edit, a `run` that regenerates files, an outside editor, /undo, /rewind) would make `edit.old` anchors fail (baseline: `table` EditError 'no match' from a stale anchor after its own previous edit, :234-236) and mislead Jev's risk stage; invalidation must key on changedFiles from git status (engine.ts:2241 refresh) plus mtime/sha at read time, and must handle files > 16 KiB (cache the clipped view with its truncatedBytes) and files removed (`context: could not read`, context.ts:114).

Loop detection stays correct only if signatures still come from the StepRecord (loopdetect.ts) — but a richer history changes behaviour: repeated identical `read`s (read:<sha12(sorted paths)>) currently trip at 3; a file cache that makes re-reads unnecessary removes that trip path, while a summary that mentions earlier failures could make the generator repeat `run` commands whose signature ignores output text. Keep `loop.lastOutcomes` semantics if WINDOW_SIZE changes (engine.ts:2081).

Compaction must never rewrite committed truth: steps.jsonl is the commit ledger (§9.1), state.json the sole resume truth, the transcript line-for-line identical across writers (TUI-DESIGN §15.1 F13). A summary is a new additive field/artefact, emitted as a transcript item, never an edit of past records; on resume the summary and the window must agree on `state.step`.

Human directives and AGENTS.md are raw by design (task and steers reach the generator unredacted, TUI-DESIGN §10.2 A156) while everything persisted is redacted — a summary generated from the raw prompt and then persisted must pass redact; a summary generated by the generator itself (an LLM call) costs a full GLM round trip (p50 12–26 s live) and can itself be malformed — prefer code-computed digests.

synthState is the synthesizer's (jev-only/llm-jev) and is dropped whole when > 64 KiB (engine.ts:1805-1806) — storing a compaction summary there would compete with `tried`/round caches and could silently erase both; use a separate bounded field.

The `done` path already depends on out-of-window memory (`lastTestRunOutput`, state.ts:447-470) that is not checkpointed: a resumed run judging `done` sees only the 600-char window tail or null; any policy that widens what the generator remembers should also make this backstop durable or Jev's completion Noul sees less than the generator does.

Terminal geometry: a context meter segment competes for status-line width (segments are dropped at narrow widths, lines.ts:540 drops 'tokens' then 'run'); at 80 columns only step/run/sess fit — the meter needs a /context or /cost row fallback, not just a status segment.
reusable: Mechanism A — full history on disk + rolling code-computed digest in the prompt. Disk: steps.jsonl (already), plus a new redacted `outputs/<step>.txt` for `read`/`run` output (≤ 60 KB / 200 KB, written at commit, plain append, ~0.1 ms). Prompt: a `## Earlier steps (digest)` section of one line per step older than the window — `step n: <action summary> → <outcome> [tests p/f/e] [changed a.py]` ≤ 160 chars — built from WindowEntry-like facts already in the StepRecord; 40 steps ≈ 6.4k chars ≈ 1.6k tokens ≈ $0.00024/step on GLM, $0.003 on Sonnet; zero extra round trips; survives resume by folding steps.jsonl (extend foldStepRecord, window.ts:74). Cost: prompt size only; no LLM summary call (a GLM summary call would add 12–26 s p50 and a 27 % malformed risk).

Mechanism B — graded tool-output retention with on-demand expansion. Keep the newest step's output at e.g. headTail(6,000, 2,000) and older window steps at 400/200 (change buildWindowEntry to take per-age bounds; window.ts:32-52), and let the generator re-open an earlier output without re-running: cheapest contract-safe form is a `read` of a virtual path `.jevcode/outputs/<step>` served from the outputs artefact (execute.ts read branch + resolveInside allow-list), signature read:<paths> unchanged, risk stage sees a read. Cost: newest-step 8k chars ≈ 2k tokens ≈ $0.0003/step GLM; expansion is one step (one GLM call) instead of a re-run of tests (0.1–100 s) — still a step, so pair with Mechanism C to avoid needing it for files.

Mechanism C — file-content cache in the prompt (the direct fix for baseline finding 3). Engine-owned Map<path, {content (≤ 16 KiB view, redacted), bytes, truncatedBytes, sha/mtime, shownAtStep}> filled from context-stage reads (context.ts:104-109) and `read` actions (execute.ts:64-80); rendered as `## Files you have seen (current)` in every mode incl. jev-off and llm-jev generic; entries invalidated when the path appears in changedFiles (edit/write/patch targets at commit, git status after `run`) and refreshed from disk at next prompt (workspace.read, sub-ms) so the generator always sees the post-edit file instead of re-reading it. Bound: reuse PROMPT_LIMITS.contextTotalBytes 61,440 / 12 files as the default, configurable up to e.g. 256 KiB on ≥ 1M-context models; eviction LRU by shownAtStep, pinnedFiles never evicted. Cost: ≤ 15k tokens/step ≈ $0.002 GLM / $0.03 Sonnet; harness < 1 ms; state.json stores only the index (paths + sha + step), bodies re-read on resume.

Mechanism D — Jev keep/drop per item (cheap because Jev is flat in question count: 1,000 Nouls 466 ms). Piggyback one Noul per cached file / digest line onto the existing context request (same state, no extra round trip) — `keep:<path>` 'Will the engineer still need `p` on this `<intent>` step? Apply criteria.context' — and evict p < 0.3, keep ≥ 0.5, leave the band alone. Cost ≈ $0.0001–0.0005 per request at $0.042/M; constraints: §5.4 question rules (criteria both sides; the context Noul's shared `criteria.context` is the precedent, state.ts:275-292), the state must carry per-item facts only (bytes, shownAtStep, changedSince, mentionsInTask), and the request must stay under Jev's 32k context — so never send the cached bodies to Jev, only the index.

Mechanism E — compaction triggers and what compaction writes. Triggers (code): (1) token estimate of the assembled user message > `context.compactAt` (default 40 % of the model's contextLength, or 100k chars when unknown), (2) every `context.compactEverySteps` (e.g. 12), (3) on replan or a human `/compact`. Action: fold digest lines older than N into a `## Run summary` paragraph (code template: plan done/remaining deltas, files changed with step numbers, last passing/failing test counts, open harness problems) ≤ 4 KiB; write it to a new additive `CheckpointState.contextSummary?: { step, text, coveredThrough }` (redacted, bounded like synthState but separate), emit a `notice { kind: 'ui' }`/transcript line `compacted steps 1–12 into 1.9 KiB`, append a `compaction` line to sessions/index.jsonl; never touch steps.jsonl or the window. Never compact Jev's state — it is already the compaction.

Mechanism F — user-visible context meter. Source: GeneratorCallRecord.usage (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite) of the last call and a new `contextLength` column beside PRICING_TABLE (GLM 1,310,720 / 1,048,576 top-provider; Sonnet 5 1,000,000 per docs/research/07-generator-apis.md:33). Surfaces: status-line segment `ctx 18k/1.0M 2%` after 'tokens' at ≥ 160 cols (lines.ts:394, :432-441), a `/cost` row `context: last prompt 18.2k tok (files 9.1k · window 3.4k · plan 1.2k · digest 0.8k) of 1.0M`, and a `/context` command listing cached files with shownAtStep/bytes and offering `/context drop <path>` and `/context pin <path>` (writes only the in-memory index; no engine restart). Cost: code only; per-section token estimates by chars/4 are enough for a meter (exact counts arrive with usage after the call).

Existing building blocks to reuse: headTail/clip markers (src/core/text.ts:6-16, `…[N chars omitted]…`), redactJson/redactDeep (state.ts:60-67, store.ts:152-160), buildWindowEntry/pushWindow/foldStepRecord (window.ts), `shownFiles` per entry (engine.ts:2537-2541) as the seed of a file index, `PromptInput` sections assembled in buildUserMessage (prompts.ts:270-287) — add sections there so --plain/TUI/jev-off/llm-jev-generic all get them, the `notice { kind: 'ui' }` → Engine.annotate path for compaction lines (TUI-DESIGN §15.1), the additive-optional-field convention of CheckpointState (`synthState?`, `pendingDirectives?` with conditional spread, engine.ts:1467-1470), and the sessions index line kinds (`pause`, `budget`, …) for a `compaction` line.

Sizing rules a design should state explicitly: generator-side budgets scale with provider (contextLength × fraction, priced by config.generator.pricing); Jev-side budgets are fixed (STATE_LIMITS; total state ≤ ~10k tokens keeps p50 ≈ 240 ms, ≤ 30k ≈ 370 ms, hard wall 32k); harness budget for all context assembly < 5 ms/step (the gate's remaining headroom); checkpoint growth per step ≤ a few KiB (index only); every added surface redacted once at capture; every truncation visible (a note in the window entry + a transcript line), never a silent middle cut.

Test hooks that already exist and would catch regressions: the flat-tokens test on promptChars (propose.ts:27), perf/step-overhead harness gate (50 ms p95 on a 5,000-file repo with `run` steps), the mocked TUI render-lag gate, resume tests around foldStepRecord, and the bench summary's tokens/step columns (generator.jsonl) to measure the cost of any policy on the same 28-task set as the baseline (glm-jev-off-baseline.md §'The bar').
